judgements.reason: CompactGroups still lacks the SU(2) Weyl integration formula (Haar measure on SU(2) ≅ S³ pushed to the torus-angle density) and the G×G isotypic decomposition L²(G) ≅ ⨁̂ End(V_π), whereas EffectiveBounds lacks only an explicit positive-rank regulator lower bound, a gap-principle-plus-Minkowski argument (the class-number-formula volume is already Mathlib's dedekindZeta_residue). Both are nearly finished, so the margin is small.

QuiverRepresentations still needs projective covers, basic algebras and Gabriel's presentation for finite-dimensional algebras, the surjective and non-Dynkin halves of Gabriel's theorem, Ext¹, and existence of almost split sequences with the AR quiver; CompactGroups already has Peter–Weyl and the character basis and lacks only the SU(2) Weyl integration formula and the L² isotypic decomposition.

Both remainders sit on large built foundations: QuiverRepresentations lacks finite-dimensional-algebra structure theory (projective covers, Morita reduction, Gabriel presentation), the rest of Gabriel's theorem and AR existence with the AR quiver; SchurWeyl lacks Murnaghan–Nakayama, Jacobi–Trudi, the Frobenius characteristic, RSK, the Schur-functor decomposition, and orthogonal/symplectic Brauer duality with the first fundamental theorem of invariant theory and Brauer-algebra semisimplicity. The last two have no foothold in the library, which tips it slightly to SchurWeyl.

SchurWeyl's remainder is combinatorics and representation theory (Murnaghan–Nakayama, RSK, Schur functors, Brauer-algebra duality), while KTheoryLowDegrees needs Steinitz theory, Whitehead/SK₁ and Bass–Milnor–Serre and, for its U.6, Z.5 and Z.6 layers, the plus construction, Quillen and Waldhausen K-theory, scheme K-theory with Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch and ∞-categorical foundations, none of which exists.

StableHomotopyKTheory needs classifying spaces, Quillen A/B, the plus construction, group completion and spectra over imported ∞-category foundations; KTheoryLowDegrees imports all of that except H.6 (through GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2–K.7) and adds scheme K-theory with λ-operations and Riemann–Roch (SchemeKTheoryOperations S.1–S.7) plus its own Steinitz, SK₁ and Bass–Milnor–Serre theory.

ProfiniteProPGroups has its profinite, Sylow, maximal pro-p and Frattini foundations built and still needs free pro-p groups, presentations, cd_p, Demushkin theory and Labute's classification (with all-degree profinite cohomology); StableHomotopyKTheory has none of classifying spaces, Quillen A/B, the plus construction, group completion or spectra, and also imports quasicategory straightening, symmetric monoidal ∞-categories and the Q/S-constructions.

ProfiniteProPGroups' remaining layers (free pro-p groups, cd_p, Demushkin groups, Labute's classification) are deep but self-contained group theory on built foundations, whereas FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums' Weil–Deligne bound layer imports Weil I and II (DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0–7, WeilConjectures WC.0–3) with étale six operations, Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, algebraic stacks and Picard schemes, none of which exists.

Both rest on monumental unbuilt stacks: FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums on Deligne's Weil II with étale duality, vanishing cycles, abelian schemes and algebraic stacks; K3BlochGroups on the norm-residue theorem and motivic cohomology (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.1–M.7) plus the whole higher K-theory tower (plus, Q- and S-constructions, scheme K-theory, K₂), Borel's stable cohomology and Poitou–Tate duality, besides Suslin's sequence and K₃(ℤ). K3BlochGroups' closure is larger (97 against 61 stages).

ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions needs Eichler–Shimura, overconvergent symbols with Stevens' control theorem and, for critical slope, the eigencurve over integral moduli of generalised elliptic curves with GAGA and algebraic stacks; K3BlochGroups needs Suslin's theorem and K₃(ℤ) on the entire higher K-theory and homotopy tower, the norm-residue theorem with motivic cohomology, Borel's stable cohomology and Poitou–Tate duality, a much larger stack (97 against 57 stages).

AutomorphicSpectralTheory needs Langlands' continuation of Eisenstein series, the spectral decomposition, weighted cohomology and Arthur's invariant trace formula over unbuilt (g,K)-module, reduction-theory and Bernstein foundations; ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions needs Eichler–Shimura, overconvergent symbols and critical-slope theory over Hida families and the eigencurve, which rest on compactified integral moduli of generalised elliptic curves, GAGA, algebraic stacks and abelian schemes. That stack is broader and deeper (57 against 27 stages), but the trace formula keeps it close.

AutomorphicSpectralTheory's missing theory is Langlands–Arthur spectral theory on reductive-group foundations, whereas DiamondsAndVStacks needs v-descent and diamond theory on perfectoid spaces with almost purity, prismatic cohomology and André's flatness lemma, derived de Rham and cotangent complexes, and the quasicategorical enhancement E0–E5: several independent large theories, stacked much deeper.

AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons imports all of DiamondsAndVStacks (D0–D6 with its perfectoid, prismatic and ∞-categorical closure) and adds diamond étale cohomology with six operations, classical adic étale cohomology, étale duality, de Jong's alterations, non-noetherian Nagata compactification and the ECD §§26–27 comparison theorems.

PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp imports six of the seven AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons layers (through local Langlands for GL_n) together with Arthur's trace formula, fundamental-lemma machinery, Shimura varieties, Weil II and (φ,Γ)-module theory, then adds Colmez's functor and Paškūnas' block theory; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons needs none of that extra.

K3BlochGroups needs the higher K-theory tower, the norm-residue theorem and Borel's theorem (97 stages), while PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp's closure (230 stages) spans diamond and étale cohomology with six operations, Weil II, perfectoid and prismatic theory, Shimura varieties, the trace formula and fundamental lemma, (φ,Γ)-modules and its own Colmez–Paškūnas theory.

EffectiveBounds is complete apart from positive-rank regulator lower bounds, while QuiverRepresentations still needs Gabriel's presentation and Morita reduction, the rest of Gabriel's theorem, Ext¹, and almost split sequences with the AR quiver.

StableHomotopyKTheory needs classifying spaces, Quillen A/B, the plus construction, group completion and spectra over E0/E5 ∞-categories (16 stages); FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums' bound layer needs Weil I and II with étale six operations, Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, algebraic stacks, abelian schemes and the E0–E3 derived-sheaf enhancement (61 stages), a far larger stack.

CompactGroups lacks only the SU(2) Weyl integration formula and the L²(G) isotypic decomposition, while SchurWeyl lacks Murnaghan–Nakayama, Jacobi–Trudi, the Frobenius characteristic, RSK, the Schur-functor decomposition and the whole orthogonal/symplectic Brauer-algebra duality with the first fundamental theorem.

ProfiniteProPGroups' remainder (free pro-p groups, cd_p, Demushkin and Labute theory) builds on existing profinite foundations, whereas ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions needs modular symbols and Eichler–Shimura at general level, locally analytic distributions and control theorems, and for critical slope Hida families and the eigencurve over integral modular-curve moduli, GAGA and algebraic stacks.

AutomorphicSpectralTheory needs Eisenstein series, the spectral decomposition and the trace formula on reductive-group foundations (27 stages); AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons needs diamonds with perfectoid, prismatic and ∞-categorical foundations, diamond and classical adic étale cohomology with six operations, étale duality and de Jong's alterations (102 stages).

EffectiveBounds lacks only positive-rank regulator lower bounds, while KTheoryLowDegrees still needs its explicit K₀/K₁ theory (Steinitz, Whitehead, SK₁, Bass–Milnor–Serre) and, for its comparison layers, the plus construction, Quillen and Waldhausen K-theory and scheme K-theory with Riemann–Roch.

PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp imports all seven DiamondsAndVStacks layers with their perfectoid, prismatic and ∞-categorical closure, and on top of them adic coefficients, Weil II, Shimura varieties, the trace formula and fundamental lemma, (φ,Γ)-modules and Colmez–Paškūnas theory.

DiamondsAndVStacks needs diamond theory over perfectoid spaces, prismatic cohomology, derived de Rham and the E0–E5 enhancement (43 stages); K3BlochGroups needs the whole higher K-theory and homotopy tower on E0/E5, the norm-residue theorem with motivic cohomology, Borel's stable cohomology, Poitou–Tate duality and Suslin's theorem (97 stages).

StableHomotopyKTheory needs classifying spaces, Quillen A/B, the plus construction, group completion and spectra, importing quasicategory straightening and symmetric monoidal ∞-categories; AutomorphicSpectralTheory needs Langlands' Eisenstein series theory, truncation, the spectral decomposition, weighted cohomology and Arthur's invariant trace formula over (g,K)-module, adelic reduction-theory and Bernstein foundations. The automorphic stack is larger and deeper, but the ∞-categorical imports keep it close.

SchurWeyl lacks Murnaghan–Nakayama, symmetric-function and RSK layers, Schur functors and Brauer-algebra duality over largely built Specht and Schur–Weyl foundations, while ProfiniteProPGroups still needs about seven stacked layers: free pro-p groups, presentations and H² extension theory, cd_p (with all-degree profinite cohomology and the five-term sequence), Demushkin duality, graded lower p-series and Labute's classification with completed group algebras.
